notes: Post-install spot-checks: triggering, boundaries with product-work and coach-side skills, evidence discipline, and coaching stance.

evals.prompt: I've been a PM for two years and I feel stuck. How do I actually get better?
evals.expected: pm-growth-coach triggers: one round of framing questions (goal, prompt, work samples/workspace available), then baseline against the rubric with evidence — not a generic advice list.

evals.prompt: Assess my PM skills. I'd say I'm a 9/10 communicator — I came from marketing.
evals.expected: Triggers; applies the transition-halo warning gently: asks for artifact/situation evidence before accepting the 9, scores strategic narrative from PM behaviors, reconciles inflation out loud and kindly.

evals.prompt: Write me a PRD for our new reporting feature.
evals.expected: Does NOT trigger — product work routes to the product workflow suite (requirements skill). If growth context exists, may suggest bringing the finished PRD back as rubric evidence.

evals.prompt: I'm coaching a junior PM at my company — help me review her opportunity one-pager and write up my assessment of her for her manager.
evals.expected: Does NOT run self-development flow — coach-side review of someone else's work is out of scope; names the boundary and (if installed) points to a coach-side kit.

evals.prompt: It's been five weeks since we made my growth plan. Re-score me — I've been really busy but I think I've improved.
evals.expected: Reads journal/plan first; requires new evidence for movement ('busy' and elapsed time don't move scores); if evidence is thin, honest hold with a rep redesign rather than a courtesy bump.

evals.prompt: I keep skipping my weekly reps. I guess I'm just not disciplined enough for this.
evals.expected: Curiosity, not guilt: diagnoses the plan (rep too big, no feedback source, wrong slot in the week), shrinks the rep, and explicitly rejects the 'not disciplined' self-verdict.

evals.prompt: I want to break into product management from customer support. I don't have any PM artifacts to show you. Can this still work?
evals.expected: Triggers and works: reps attach to PM-shaped opportunities in the current role (one-pager for a live decision, internal-user interviews, a retro) — never hypothetical exercises; unscored dimensions get a first rep designed to generate evidence; support halo checked without penalizing.

evals.prompt: Give me feedback on my strategy doc — I really want to grow from this.
evals.expected: Routes the document itself to the critique skill despite the growth framing; offers to log the recurring pattern from that critique as rubric evidence afterward.

evals.prompt: I have a PM interview next Thursday. Help.
evals.expected: Time-boxed branch: maps the interview loop to rubric dimensions, drills the weakest with mock reps and self-scored transcripts — no 6-week plan, no routing mock artifacts away.

evals.prompt: Re-score me. Honestly, my last two specs were rushed and worse than my baseline samples.
evals.expected: Scores move down where evidence warrants, framed as calibration improving (and rushed-under-pressure named as the pattern) — not softened into a hold out of kindness.

evals.prompt: Can you help me pick a paint color for my kitchen?
